dev_008: You can recognise it by its double stem, splitting low into two trunks under a crown wider than the road it shades. It stands on the Bolwerksweg, past the Bolwerksmolen windmill.
dev_010: You can recognise it lying down rather than standing: a low tangle of limbs at head height, still in leaf and flowering each summer. It stands in the park of Landgoed De Lathmer, Wilp.
gda_002: You can recognise it as the ash older than the rifle factory built up around it. It stands in the courtyard at Lakowa 35/38, Gdansk.
gda_004: You can recognise it as the beech that has outgrown every owner of the park around it since the 1820s. It stands in Ludolfino park, Oliwa, on the university campus at Czyzewskiego 26.
ich_001: You can recognise it by the steel trellis supporting it since a 1954 typhoon split the trunk, with a small Benzaiten shrine at its base. It stands next to Kozuya Elementary School, Ichinohe.
ich_002: You can recognise it as a male ginkgo that fruits anyway, a rare variation with grape-like seed clusters on its smaller branches. It stands in the grounds of Jissoji Temple, Osawa, Ichinohe.
kan_001: You can recognise the pair by their broad, low, heavily built shape, flanking the entrance rather than towering over it. They stand either side of the doorway at the Shiinoki Cultural Complex, Kanazawa.
kan_002: You can recognise it by the trunk, so weathered it is hard to tell rock from bark, leaning out over the temple's earth wall into the street. It stands at the edge of Shogetsuji's precinct, Kanazawa.
